name: User Access Review Record
description: The complete record of a periodic entitlement review: the population reviewed, the reviewer's per-entitlement decisions, and evidence that changes flagged during the review were applied in the underlying system.

expected_content.element: Complete entitlement listing for the reviewed system, including account identifier, owner, role or permission set, and account status
expected_content.why: Establishes the population; without it the auditor cannot assess whether the review was complete.

expected_content.element: Statement of how the population was generated (system, query or report name, extraction date, filters applied)
expected_content.why: Population completeness and accuracy is assessed before any sample is drawn.

expected_content.element: Reviewer identity and review date for each section of the population
expected_content.why: Establishes that an appropriate person performed the review and when.
Distinguishes a genuine review from a bulk acknowledgement.

expected_content.element: Ticket or change record for every item flagged for modification or revocation
expected_content.why: Demonstrates follow-through; a review with no closure evidence is the most common failure of this control.

expected_content.element: Post-change confirmation from the system showing the access was actually removed or reduced
expected_content.why: Ticket closure alone does not demonstrate the entitlement changed.

expected_content.element: Inclusion of service accounts, shared accounts, contractors, and privileged roles
expected_content.why: Their omission is the most common scope defect in this evidence.

expected_content.element: Reconciliation of the population to HR records or the identity provider
expected_content.why: Strengthens the completeness assertion where the source system is not itself authoritative.

owner: System owner, coordinated by the IAM function

freshness_expectation.rationale: DriftGuard default of one quarterly cadence plus a 30-day grace window. Not an audit rule.

redaction_guidance: Personal identifiers beyond what is needed to attribute an account may be masked, provided attribution remains verifiable.
Never include credentials, secrets, API keys, or session tokens in an access review export.
retention_guidance: Retain for at least the examination period plus the duration of the subsequent examination, so the artifact remains available when tested.

validation_rules.rule: A review record exists for every scheduled review date falling within the examination period.
The reviewed population reconciles to the authoritative identity source with no unexplained omissions, including non-human and privileged accounts.
Every entitlement flagged for revocation or modification has a corresponding closure record with post-change system confirmation.
Each review was completed within the cadence defined by the organization's own policy.
The population is a system-generated export with a stated generation method, not a manually maintained list.
The reviewed system is within the declared system boundary for the examination.

common_issues.issue: Reviewer signs off the whole listing without recording per-entitlement decisions.
common_issues.impact: The auditor cannot distinguish a review from an acknowledgement; the control's detective purpose is unevidenced.

common_issues.issue: Population drawn from a single application export, omitting a secondary identity provider or contractor directory.
common_issues.impact: Accounts outside the export were never reviewed, so the control does not cover its intended scope.

common_issues.issue: Items flagged for revocation are recorded but never closed, or closed only in the ticket.
common_issues.impact: The access identified as inappropriate remained live.

common_issues.issue: Review conducted after fieldwork began, covering a period already elapsed.
common_issues.impact: The control did not operate during the period as described.

source_refs.supports: Expected content, persuasiveness weighting, and the common issues list.

notes: No SOC 2 criterion prescribes the format or contents of an access review record. This definition is DriftGuard's model of what makes the artifact persuasive.
The entitlement listing is system-generated; the per-entitlement decision is a human judgement recorded against it.
Backfilled with evidence_role and origin in the CC6 phase (schema 0.2.0). Content otherwise unchanged.
